proof.text: Write $A=\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$, $B=\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$ and $C=\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V}^{\mathrm{ess}\mathcal U}$. For $X,Y\in A$, the sets $\operatorname{Hom}(X\times\Delta^n,Y)$ are unchanged on passing from $\mathcal U$ to $\mathcal V$: a simplicial map is the same family of component functions satisfying the same identities in either universe. These sets and their simplicial operators lie in $\mathcal U$ by closure of a Grothendieck universe under the relevant products and subsets. Thus $A(X,Y)=B(X,Y)=C(X,Y)$, with the same composition and units. For any $X,Y\in B$, [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan] applies because $Y$ is Kan and $X$ is a simplicial set in $\mathcal V$; hence $B(X,Y)$ is Kan. Its restrictions show that $A$ and $C$ are locally Kan too. The inclusion $i:A\hookrightarrow C$ is therefore an isomorphism on each mapping simplicial set. Consequently their coherent nerves are quasicategories by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison].

source.place: Definition 1.2.16.1 and Remarks 1.2.16.2 and 1.2.16.4; Kerodon Corollary 3.1.3.4 (00TN).

proof.text: For a weak homotopy equivalence $f:X\to Y$ of $\mathcal V$-small Kan complexes, [lem-coef-kan-weak-equivalence-space-edge] gives an inverse map and both inverse-triangle witnesses in $N_{\mathrm{hc}}B$. Thus the actual edge $f$ is an equivalence. This also handles the zigzag interpretation of "weakly homotopy equivalent." Indeed, factor every terminal map in $\mathcal V$-small simplicial sets using the functorial Kan model structure [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], obtaining $T\xrightarrow{r_T}RT$ with $r_T$ weak and $RT$ Kan. Naturality and two-out-of-three make $Rf$ weak for every weak map $f$. A finite zigzag can consequently be replaced by a zigzag of Kan complexes, and the original Kan endpoints are linked to their replacements by $r_X,r_Y$. All these objects remain $\mathcal V$-small. Apply the preceding edge result to each arrow. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], equivalence edges are exactly invertible morphisms of the homotopy category, so inverses and composites of these morphisms give an equivalence between the endpoints. In particular every object of $C$ is equivalent in $N_{\mathrm{hc}}B$ to an object of $A$.

source.place: Kan-space edge comparison; functorial Kan replacement and two-out-of-three from the cited Kan-model statement; composition and inverse characterization from the cited homotopy-category statement. Agent expansion for finite zigzags.

proof.text: Conversely, let an edge $f:X\to Y$ be an equivalence in $N_{\mathrm{hc}}B$. By the definition of equivalence in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], there are an inverse edge $g:Y\to X$ and inverse triangles. Edges of this coherent nerve are actual simplicial maps. For a triangle, $\mathfrak C[\Delta^2](0,2)$ is the nerve of $\{\{0,2\}\subset\{0,1,2\}\}$, hence $\Delta^1$. Its image in $B(X,X)$ has endpoints $1_X$ and $gf$, because composition in the thickening is union; the second triangle similarly gives endpoints $1_Y$ and $fg$ in $B(Y,Y)$. By the internal-functor formula these are maps $X\times\Delta^1\to X$ and $Y\times\Delta^1\to Y$ with precisely those endpoint restrictions. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak], which allows either endpoint orientation, to conclude that $f$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This computation uses only the two subsets defining the triangle, not a general comparison lemma left implicit.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.6.10; explicit subset-poset triangle computation. Realization of the resulting homotopies: Kerodon Construction 3.6.5.1 (0148).

proof.text: By Step 1, $\pi_0i$ is fully faithful. For $X\in C$, choose $K\in A$ and the equivalence between $X$ and $K$ from Step 2. Its inverse triangles, computed as in Step 3, give the equations $[g][f]=1$ and $[f][g]=1$ on components of the enriched mapping sets. Since $C$ is full and both endpoints belong to $C$, all the maps and paths in these equations belong to $C$. Thus $X$ is isomorphic to $iK$ in $\pi_0C$, so $\pi_0i$ is essentially surjective. Together with the isomorphisms on mapping simplicial sets in Step 1, this is exactly the definition of a Dwyer--Kan equivalence in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison].

source.place: Sections 1.1.4-1.1.5; direct verification of the Dwyer--Kan conditions, using the definition in the cited node.

proof.text: The coherent nerve of $C$ is the full simplicial subset of $N_{\mathrm{hc}}B$ on its objects. In fact, an $n$-simplex is a simplicial functor $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to B$. It factors uniquely through the full simplicial subcategory $C$ if and only if its $n+1$ object values lie in $C$: all its mapping maps then already have the required targets, since the mapping sets of $C$ are the same as those of $B$. This criterion is preserved by restriction along every monotone map, hence identifies the entire simplicial subset, not only its vertices or edges. The full-subcategory convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] is exactly this vertex condition.

source.place: Section 1.2.11 and the subset-poset coherent-nerve formula in Section 1.1.5; direct degreewise factorization.

proof.text: Let $E$ be the object class of the full replete essential image of $N_{\mathrm{hc}}A\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}B$: its objects are those equivalent to a $\mathcal U$-small Kan complex. Step 2 shows $\operatorname{Ob}(C)\subset E$. If $X\in E$, an equivalence edge between $X$ and some $K\in A$ is an actual simplicial map and is weak by Step 3, proving $X\in C$. Consequently $E=\operatorname{Ob}(C)$. This class is closed under equivalences: in the homotopy category of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], compose the given isomorphism $X\cong K$ with an isomorphism $X\cong Y$ (inverting it when necessary); the result is an isomorphism $Y\cong K$, represented by an equivalence edge by that same statement. Step 5 now identifies $N_{\mathrm{hc}}C$ with exactly the full replete subcategory specified in the conclusion.

source.place: Remark 1.2.16.4 and Section 1.2.11; explicit identification of object classes using Steps 2 and 3.

proof.text: All three coherent nerves are quasicategories by local Kan-ness in Step 1 and [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Apply its natural mapping-space comparisons to the enriched inclusion $A\to B$. For $X,Y\in A$ they identify the induced mapping-space map with the identity $A(X,Y)=B(X,Y)$ from Step 1, up to the specified natural equivalences; hence $J:N_{\mathrm{hc}}A\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}B$ is fully faithful. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] in the further universe containing both entire categories: it supplies a coherent quasi-inverse and both coherent natural equivalences for the restriction of $J$ to its full replete essential image. By Steps 5 and 6 that restriction is precisely $N_{\mathrm{hc}}i:N_{\mathrm{hc}}A\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}C$. Since the left side is $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ by the stipulated Kan-space model, this is the asserted equivalence, induced by the original inclusion.

source.place: Theorem 4.8.4.1; natural mapping-space comparison is HTT Proposition 2.2.4.1 and Theorem 2.2.0.1, as stated by the cited coherent-nerve node.

title: Universe change for essentially small Kan complexes
statement: Use spaces, weak homotopy equivalences and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], locally Kan simplicial categories, Dwyer--Kan equivalences and coherent nerves of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and the Kan-enriched model of spaces of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ and perform constructions involving whole categories in a further containing universe. Let $\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ and $\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$ be the simplicial categories of Kan complexes in the indicated universes, with $n$-simplices in their mapping complexes the maps $X\times\Delta^n\to Y$. Let $\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V}^{\mathrm{ess}\mathcal U}$ be the full simplicial subcategory on those $\mathcal V$-small Kan complexes weakly homotopy equivalent to $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes. The enriched inclusion $\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V}^{\mathrm{ess}\mathcal U}$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Its coherent nerve is an equivalence $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V}^{\mathrm{ess}\mathcal U})$, where $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U})$; the latter nerve is the full replete subcategory of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal V})$ on spaces equivalent to $\mathcal U$-small ones.
